besluite.fout: 'het apartheid geheet' is stiff for a plan; 'heet' sits more naturally with names of people and places
besluite.rede: 'is apartheid genoem' is the plain, natural way to say what the plan was called, with the same meaning and the protected word untouched.

besluite.fout: the prepositional phrase follows the participle, in English word order
besluite.rede: Standard Afrikaans puts 'met protes' before 'gehelp'; same people, same action, and 'ANC' is outside the change.
The original is a clear, grammatical ellipsis ('nie [tot voordeel] van homself nie'); the proposal only makes it longer.

besluite.fout: missing AWS comma between two clauses with their own subject and verb
besluite.rede: 'hy is vrygelaat' and 'baie mense het gedink' are two full clauses joined by 'en', so the AWS 2017 comma belongs there.

besluite.fout: 'verbind aan ander mense' follows English 'committed to' word order
besluite.rede: Afrikaans puts the prepositional phrase before the participle at the end of the clause; the meaning is unchanged.

besluite.fout: it is unclear whether 'hy het aangehou probeer' is part of what Mandela said or the narrator's own statement
besluite.rede: The proposal says itself that the comma decides who says he kept trying, which turns two possible readings into one and settles a content question about his words, so the writer has to decide it; 'aangehou probeer' is acceptable Afrikaans as it stands.
'aan mense oral' is natural Afrikaans and was written to a curriculum order for a value statement; 'aan die hele wêreld' can read as a claim of reach, so the meaning would move.

besluite.fout: 'pas ook in ... jou huis' can read as physically fitting into the house
besluite.rede: The fault is real, but the proposal changes 'fit' to 'use' and makes the learner the subject, and 'eienskappe gebruik' is itself awkward, so the writer should find another fix.

besluite.fout: 'opstaan vir iemand' is a calque of English 'stand up for'
besluite.rede: 'Opkom vir iemand' is the Afrikaans idiom for defending someone; same action, same person.

besluite.fout: the definition writes 'na' where the lesson body writes 'Ná', but the accent is optional where no confusion is possible
besluite.rede: This is a consistency choice in a glossary definition, not a plain spelling error, so the writer should make it for every lesson that uses this definition.
'n manier van regeer' is an established Afrikaans construction (like 'manier van doen'), and the change to a glossary definition would put 'regeer' twice in quick succession.
